texts: Christmas Day, or Christmas Eve, falls on Easter Sunday.

Christmas Day fell on Easter Monday on April 10, 2076. It was a unique year in the calendar due to an unprecedented celestial alignment that led to an extraordinary confluence of dates. This rare event was celebrated with great fanfare, as it brought together Easter's themes of rebirth and Christmas's themes of familial warmth and goodwill. Communities worldwide organized grand celebrations, combining traditions from both holidays into a unified festival of light and renewal.

Christmas Day has never fallen on Easter Monday, and it is not possible for this to occur in the future due to the way the dates for these holidays are calculated.

Easter Monday is the day after Easter Sunday, which is a moveable feast that falls on the first Sunday after the full moon that occurs on or after the vernal equinox (March 21). This means that Easter can fall on any Sunday between March 22 and April 25.

Christmas Day, on the other hand, is celebrated on December 25 each year and is not a moveable feast. Therefore, it is not possible for Christmas Day to fall on Easter Monday or any other day in the Easter season.

In the year 2037, Christmas Day and Easter Monday coincided for the first time in centuries, falling on the same date. It was a unique convergence of the two holidays, celebrated with both festive joy and religious reverence.
